When a Pet Dies

Open this in the first days after a pet dies, when the house is the wrong kind of quiet and you are not sure you are allowed to grieve this much. It gives the loss its proper size and a few gentle things to do.

Pet Loss · Grief · Loss · Self-Compassion · 8 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Say out loud that this is a real loss — Naming it stops you arguing with yourself about whether it counts.
  • Keep one thing of theirs in sight — A collar or a bowl on the shelf gives the grief somewhere to sit.
  • Tell one person who knew the two of you — Being heard by someone who knew them beats general sympathy.
  • Expect the routine to be the hardest part — The empty hour at feeding time catches almost everyone.
  • Let yourself cry at the walk you skip — Grief for an animal arrives through habits more than thoughts.
  • Write down one ordinary memory — The small daily things fade first and are what you will want back.
  • Call or text 988 if you stop wanting to be here — Free, confidential help is there at any hour, and reaching for it is a strong move.
  • Decide about another pet later, not now — A choice made in the first week is made by the grief, not by you.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
